newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Representative introduces new IRA tax bill.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Representative introduces new IRA tax bill.

text.p: A leading member of the tax-writing House Ways and Means committee said Monday he introduced legislation to expand tax-deferred Individual Retirement Accounts and create a new type of IRA.
The measure, sponsored by California Republican Rep. Bill Thomas, would remove income caps that prevent many people from making tax-deductible contributions to IRAs.

Current law allows only taxpayers who are not covered by other pension arrangements and whose income does not exceed $40,000 for couples and $25,000 for singles to be eligible for a fully deductible IRA. Those income limits would be phased out over a four-year period, beginning in 1997.

The bill would also create a new "IRA plus" account. Contributions to such an account would not be tax-deductible, but earnings would be tax-free after five years if the IRA-holder is at least 59 and a half years old.
Funds could be withdrawn, penalty free, from either type of IRA to pay for education, a home or other family expenses during periods of long-term unemployment.
The $2,000 per year contribution limit to IRAs would be indexed for inflation.
